Alex P.: Heads-up — after the batching-heuristics tweak merged yesterday I'm seeing steady RSS growth on long-context runs (>>16k tokens). Not a hard crash yet but memory keeps climbing across requests.
Maria G.: ugh. which change specifically? the 'prefer-small-batches' flag?
Alex P.: yeah, that flag + a kernel selection fallback I added for certain attention widths. I haven't bisected fully yet.
Samir: can you paste the repro command? I can run a synthetic harness.
Alex P.: repro: `./bench/kv_longflow --model=redwood-tiny --seq=65536 --batch=1 --requests=200 --seed=42 --enable-prefetch` — workload is concatenated long-context docs. Attached a small trace: `kvcache_live_entries: 412k`, `evictions_total: 23k`, `reused_segments: 6k`, RSS delta: +1.8GB over ~90s.
Maria G.: hmm evictions seem high relative to entries. fragmentation?
Alex P.: profiler snapshot: `kvcache_allocs: hot=0.72, cold=0.28`, allocator fragmentation metric shows ~22% free but unusable (small slabs). Also saw repeated allocate/free hotspots around segment_size=2048.
Samir: could be the kernel change altered typical per-step KV write patterns so we end up with many small allocations. I hit similar in the LRU compaction experiment last quarter.
DevOps-Bot: perf-bot uploaded artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/artifacts/1815001234/ (kvcache-snap.tar.gz, heap-prof.txt, evict-log.txt)
Maria G.: can someone run the regression harness with the old heuristics vs new heuristics and diff the evict traces? I'd like both runs with `--deterministic` and `--log-allocs`.
Samir: running now (on a dedicated node). Command I'm using:
```
./bench/kv_longflow \
  --model=redwood-tiny \
  --seq=65536 \
  --batch=1 \
  --requests=500 \
  --deterministic \
  --log-allocs \
  --output=/tmp/kv-1815001234
```
Samir: quick note: for long-context suites we should bump GC pressure by varying prefix reuse ratio. otherwise cache reuse hides fragmentation.
Alex P.: good call. My synthetic had 100% new prefixes which stresses evictions but maybe masks reuse. I'll re-run with 60/40 reuse.
Maria G.: also add a CI regression that runs a short form (seq=32k, requests=50) and checks that RSS delta < 400MB and evictions_per_request < 200. That should catch the growth.
Samir: initial run finished. Summary (new heuristics): `peak_rss=7.1GB`, `start_rss=4.2GB`, `rss_delta=2.9GB`, `evictions=48.2k`, `reused=4.1k`, `alloc-frag=26%`.
Samir: old heuristics run: `peak_rss=5.0GB`, `start_rss=4.1GB`, `rss_delta=0.9GB`, `evictions=12.5k`, `reused=15.4k`, `alloc-frag=9%`.
Maria G.: that's a solid regression. Looks like new kernel selection reduced reuse significantly leading to more churn.
Alex P.: interesting: kernel selection chooses a narrow attention kernel for certain shapes which writes KV in smaller segment sizes; combined with changed batching we probably increased allocation churn. I can sketch a patch to prefer larger contiguous segment allocations for writes >= 1024 tokens.
Samir: let's add a controlled test to the regression harness that exercises segment_size boundaries (512/1024/2048) and asserts reused_segments_ratio > 0.15 for 1024+.
DevOps-Bot: created ticket PERF-842: "kvcache fragmentation/regression after batching heuristic change" with links to artifacts.
Maria G.: for now let's roll back the batching tweak on canary and keep the kernel change behind a feature flag until we fix allocator behavior.
Alex P.: agreed. I'll open a PR that gates the heuristics per-deployment and add the new regression into nightly long-context-suite.
Samir: also instrument more granular per-segment lifecycle metrics (alloc_time, reuse_count) so we can pinpoint fragmentation sources without full heap profiles every time.
Maria G.: filing follow-ups: add CI check, nightly job, and perf dashboard panel for "kvcache.alloc_frag_pct".
Alex P.: thanks all — will post updates once I have a reproduce+fix PR. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: reaction :rocket: on message from Alex P.
